quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: David Samson on the difficulty of negotiating with Daktronics
quotes.excerpt: It's a far way from the Rocksbury.
quotes.quote: It's a far way from the Rocksbury.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: David Samson on the Clippers' failure to address Aspiration deal
quotes.excerpt: When I told you that I was going away, your first concern was, will you be away when the NBA rules.
quotes.quote: I should warn you though, Pablo, just before you show me documents, is that when I told you that I was going away, your first concern was, will you be away when the NBA rules on Aspiration and the Clippers? That was like your number one, and we did not see a scenario by which that wouldn't have happened. Here we are, still hasn't happened.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: David Samson on why Daktronics doesn't need a crisis PR firm
quotes.excerpt: Daktronics does not require a crisis PR firm on an ongoing basis.
quotes.quote: My reaction to the episode is that Daktronics does not require a crisis PR firm on an ongoing basis. I would assume they go crisis by crisis, and they realized very quickly upon your inquiries that they needed one.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: David Samson on the danger of multiple statements
quotes.excerpt: Multiple statements can really hurt you.
quotes.quote: What surprises me is that he took a position. It's one thing the crisis PR firm will tell you, and we talk about this often, is that multiple statements can really hurt you. And he took a very strong position right after our first episode of September 3rd, and he's been walking it back slowly ever since, and it's sort of going up and down like a mountainous range of false statements.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: David Samson on the business of Daktronics and Steve Ballmer
quotes.excerpt: It's the reason why Wachtell is in business and why they've billed millions of dollars to Ballmer.
quotes.quote: It's the reason why Wachtell is in business and why they've billed millions of dollars to Ballmer, who actually pays for the NBA investigation. Side note is that Wachtell has to figure out whether or not that needle was threaded, because they're looking at the actual facts, they're interviewing witnesses.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: David Samson on how Daktronics deals are negotiated
quotes.excerpt: It is out of the question that Daktronics would have come to us and said, hey.
quotes.quote: It is out of the question that Daktronics would have come to us and said, hey, we'd love to talk to Carlos Stanton about possibly being a sponsor. We started with Daktronics when the ballpark was being built, because that's how you build the ballpark is you go to all the subcontractors and you talk about who's going to do the seats, who's going to do the toilets.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: David Samson on player involvement in Daktronics deals
quotes.excerpt: The number of times a player came up was zero.
quotes.quote: And in all of the dealings with Daktronics, the number of times a player came up was zero.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: David Samson on why he wouldn't bother an owner with small deals
quotes.excerpt: I wouldn't bother our owner with a guy who was getting a car to do a quick car deal.
quotes.quote: I wouldn't bother our owner with a guy who was getting a car to do a quick car deal, but if it were a high six, low seven figure deal, the owner would know that because I would tell him.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: David Samson on how to manipulate contract budgets
quotes.excerpt: You can have Daktronics change what they're charging me for the ribbon boards.
quotes.quote: I can have Daktronics change what they're charging me for the ribbon boards, and I can then save that money elsewhere or get Daktronics to spend that money on something else. It's totally legal, totally above board, but it's all a negotiation.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: David Samson on the Clippers' knowledge of the Daktronics deal
quotes.excerpt: It's 100% guaranteed that the Clippers had to know about it.
quotes.quote: I'm not saying it's 95, Pablo. It's 100% guaranteed that the Clippers had to know about it, and it was 100% baked in to the contract that Daktronics would have done with the Clippers to build into a dome.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: David Samson on the importance of being a stickler for details
quotes.excerpt: We're sticklers, and so just want to acknowledge that.
quotes.quote: We're sticklers, and so just want to acknowledge that.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: David Samson on when to involve an agent in player deals
quotes.excerpt: The only time we involve their agent is if the player's not being cooperative.
quotes.quote: When we're dealing with players and we are trying to get them to do things, the only time we involve their agent is if the player's not being cooperative by fulfilling what they're contractually obligated to do. But in advance, we would not bring the agent in unless it were an epic situation of discomfort between us and the player, and that was extraordinarily rare, if ever.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: David Samson on the protocol for contacting sponsors
quotes.excerpt: We would never email the sponsor to wake the sleeping dog.
quotes.quote: We would never email the sponsor to wake the sleeping dog. You generally would speak to your partners if they've contacted you first and said, dude, we paid and we can't get our signed stuff, we can't get in touch with the player. The emails would go the other way. Those I've received plenty of. I never would have an outgoing email, hey, did you reach the player?

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: David Samson on the importance of Steve Ballmer's statements
quotes.excerpt: I think it's important to go back to what Ballmer said when he talks about they're off to the races.
quotes.quote: I think it's important to go back to what Ballmer said when he talks about they're off to the races on on their own. We weren't involved. That expression does not come with all of these email chains. They are in the starting gate, it would appear.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: David Samson on the typical deliverables for player appearance deals
quotes.excerpt: You would get annually, sometimes you can do it twice a year, there'd be a signing.
quotes.quote: You would get annually, sometimes you can do it twice a year, there'd be a signing, and you could get five dozen baseballs, two dozen bats, and two appearances not to last longer than 15 to 25 minutes. And if it's a seven figure deal, you may get a private meet and greet with executives, again, not to be more than 10 people at a time. You could get a player to agree to a step and repeat if it's a mid six figure deal.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: David Samson on the complexity of stadium construction
quotes.excerpt: Anyone who says it's easy to get a ballpark done and built, it's just not.
quotes.quote: Anyone who says it's easy to get a ballpark done and built, it's just not. Try renovating your bathroom at your house. You're going to be over budget and you're not going to be on time.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: David Samson on the legality of contract manipulation
quotes.excerpt: You can absolutely manipulate contracts in order and it's totally legal, totally above board.
quotes.quote: You can absolutely manipulate contracts in order and it's totally legal, totally above board, but it's all a negotiation.
